output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and sends anything larger to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred there rose from 7% to 54% overnight that week. Referred calls resolve at about 34%, against 82% for the rest, and that matches the site-wide drop. The referral rate is the same for new and tenured agents (56%, 54% and 53%), and tenured agents fell about 8 points too. So the April intake is not the cause. The tariff increase shifted the call mix, but tariff calls resolve well. I did not check the IVR or workload explanations directly. They look minor, but they are not fully ruled out. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis. Don't start performance plans. They would punish the wrong group. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Use post-call sampling and track FCR and unsupported credits. Hold off on a site-wide restore until the trial reports. Also ask Management Information to produce the breakdown by referral status for the trial teams. It can do this within a day.
